name: XP Inc.
sector: Finance / Capital markets — Brazilian investment platform
moat_justification: Scale distribution (18.4k advisors, R$2.2tn client assets) and a two-decade brand produce durable ~20-25% ROE, but advisors are not captive, take rates compress ~5bp/yr, and banks/fintechs with bigger balance sheets contest every product line — a moderate moat, not a wide one. Measured ROIC history is unavailable (roic_proxy is null: the IFRS filer tags no operating income), so the score rests on sustained ROE rather than a computed ROIC series.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 21 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2022, 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency BRL converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (XP Inc. Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-29), cover page: securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) are 'Class A common shares, par value US$0.00001 per share — XP — The NASDAQ Global Select Market'; no ADS class is registered) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (11.0%) vs bull-case tier B (18.4%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality Brazilian investment platform, moat 6/10 — at $29.26 it does not clear 15% on the scored numbers (weighted IRR 14.4%, weighted IV@15% $27.71; it clears 15% only below $27.71), and the finance-sector OE model plus a stale FY2024 base cap confidence at low — size it to the bear end (Tier C).
moat_for: Brazil's leading independent investment platform: ~R$2.2tn client assets (AUM+AUA, 2Q26, +17% YoY), 4.8M active clients
Largest advisor distribution network in Brazil (~18.4k advisors) — distribution scale rivals cannot replicate quickly
Sustained ROE ~20-25% (22.5% in 2Q26; FY ROE 20-25% across 2020-2024 in fundamentals.json) on a capital-light model
Diversifying beyond brokerage: wholesale banking +32% YoY in 2Q26, cards, credit (loan book R$78bn, +16%), insurance, retirement (R$101bn, +18%)
Brand and investor-education franchise built over two decades in a market structurally shifting from bank deposits to investments
moat_against: Advisor network is not captive — independent advisors can multi-home or leave, and internal/RIA migration is still in progress
Take-rate compression is structural: annualized retail take rate fell 5bp YoY to 1.20% in 2Q26 as banks and fintechs compete
Entrenched banks (Itaú, BTG Pactual, Bradesco) and Nubank/Inter attack with bigger balance sheets and customer bases
Earnings geared to Brazilian rates, market volumes and BRL — USD returns carry unhedged currency risk
Revenue still concentrated in Brazilian retail investing; core wealth segment maturing (~16% share)
